items.title: A Cross-Domain Evaluation of Prompting Techniques for Large Language Models
items.title_zh: 大语言模型提示技术的跨领域评估
items.raw_content: The paper compares zero-shot prompting, few-shot prompting, RAG and a PE2-inspired automatic prompt optimization pipeline using the same LLM across six benchmark datasets covering arithmetic, logical and commonsense reasoning plus factual verification. No strategy consistently won across domains and pairwise comparisons of the best configurations showed no significant differences; RAG had the highest average accuracy at 78.33% with 300 retrieval examples.

items.title: CAT-RAG: Improving Secure Code Generation with Category-Aware Agentic Retrieval
items.title_zh: CAT-RAG：用类别感知的智能体检索改进安全代码生成
items.raw_content: CAT-RAG replaces CWE-level retrieval with compact, language-specific security categories chosen by an LLM categorizer agent, and can act as a standalone security layer or a drop-in add-on to retrieval-augmented code generation. On CyberSecEval it nearly doubles the secure-code improvement over the prior state of the art (23.57% vs. 12.11%) while reducing token overhead by 41.71%.

items.title: LLM-Based Evaluation Planning for Heterogeneous Optimization
items.raw_content:
Authors: Nian Ran, Sebastian Brulin, Markus Olhofer, Mauricio A. Álvarez, Richard Allmendinger

Heterogeneous optimization problems require an optimizer to decide not only which candidate solutions to evaluate, but also which objectives and constraints should be evaluated under different costs and fidelities. Existing SOTA methods such as MFE-NSGA-III address this setting with manually designed selection metrics, but their behavior is largely determined by predefined heuristic rules and hyperparameters. In this work, we propose REP-HO, a reasoning-based evaluation planner that replaces the rule-based mixed-fidelity selection step with a large language model (LLM) planner. The LLM receives the same primitive optimization-state information as the heuristic planner, such as surrogate predictions, uncertainties, evaluation costs, and budget status. We first show that REP-HO achieves competitive performance compared to the human-designed metric-based method (MFE-NSGA-III). We then further enhance each decision with an adaptive nearest-neighbor summary, leading to better and more stable results. We evaluate REP-HO across five heterogeneous regimes covering cost imbalance, constraint difficulty, surrogate fidelity, budget level, and objective conflict. Across these regimes, one of the two variants obtains the best mean ranking score in every regime, REP-HO(Deepseek) is first or second throughout, and the planner shows adaptive allocation behavior, such as prioritizing constraint evaluations under tighter budgets and reallocating constraint evaluation budget when surrogate reliability changes. These results suggest that LLMs can serve as flexible evaluation planners for heterogeneous optimization, offering a general alternative to fixed hand-designed metrics.

items.title: Measuring Data Diversity with Embeddings: A Taxonomy and Benchmark for Diversity Measures
items.title_zh: 用嵌入衡量数据多样性：多样性度量的分类与基准
items.raw_content: The authors present a taxonomy of 21 embedding-based diversity measures grouped into four families and introduce EmbDivBench, which evaluates them on variety, balance and disparity using simulated and natural text. Mean Pairwise Distance, the most commonly used measure, was outperformed on those components, with Graph Entropy the best overall choice.

items.title: Where Natural Language Ends in Agents: Executable Skill Composition with MetaSkill
items.raw_content:
Authors: Meng Shu, Wei He, Hang Zhou, Runke Liu, Kai Han et al.

Agent Skills express open-ended task knowledge in natural language, but composing them requires persistent execution order and upstream-output handoffs. We propose selective formalization at Skill boundaries: coordination relations with stable references and machine-checkable constraints become executable, while substantive task judgments remain within Skills. We introduce MetaSkill, a hybrid representation that preserves complete Skill packages and local instructions while making invocation dependencies and predecessor-text bindings executable through a directed acyclic graph (DAG) runtime. This interface supports explicit coordination without prescribing how each Skill performs its local task. Across 20 multi-Skill artifact tasks and two LLMs, we compare natural-language procedures, prompt-visible graphs, and MetaSkill derived from a common frozen plan per task, using the same designated Skill packages. Additional comparisons evaluate AgentSkillOS with the same available Skill packages as MetaSkill, as well as agent systems using their configured tools. Blinded artifact judgments yield favorable preference point estimates across all reported comparisons, with 95% task-bootstrap intervals excluding parity against Prompt Graph under DeepSeek-V4-Flash and OpenClaw under GLM-5.2. In audited GLM-5.2 execution traces, all planned nodes complete and all declared precedence constraints are satisfied. Together, these findings support MetaSkill as a practical interface for composing open-ended Skills, combining local linguistic flexibility with executable dependencies, explicit predecessor-text bindings, and auditable coordination. Code is available at: https://github.com/TokenRhythm/opensquilla/tree/paper/metaskill-lp4fm-2026

items.title: An Impossibility Result for ETF Target Geometry, and an Equinorm Remedy for Imbalanced Analytic Continual Learning
items.raw_content:
Authors: Berk Sezer

Analytic continual learning (ACL) methods such as ACIL and GACL fit a ridge-regression classifier head on frozen features via the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury identity, achieving exemplar-free, exact updates. A separate line of work, Progressive Neural Collapse (ProNC), shows standard continual classifiers benefit from a progressively expanding Simplex Equiangular Tight Frame (ETF) target. It is natural to ask whether fusing the two ideas, exact analytic updates and ETF targets, would yield a better closed-form continual learner. We show this is not the case as the fusion turns out to be identical to plain one-hot ACIL. Further, Simplex ETFs are not nested across class counts, so the literal "progressively expand the ETF" construction stops yielding an ETF as new tasks arrive, and it introduces catastrophic forgetting ($4\times$ that of a classic ACIL head). We therefore separate an ETF's two defining properties, equiangularity and equinormality, and apply each on its own to the classifier weights rather than the targets, where the invariance above does not hold. Equinorm post-processing of the fitted weights recovers both tail-class and overall average accuracy across the long-tailed regime from 5:1 to 100:1 imbalance (e.g. +32.0 tail-accuracy points and +16.0 average-accuracy points at 100:1 on CIFAR-100/ViT), transferring in sign across two backbones and two datasets, at a mild cost of 5.4 average-accuracy points on CIFAR-100/ViT on near-balanced streams (below $\approx 3{:}1$). Equiangular geometry, by contrast, is exactly inert on the target side but actively harmful on the weight side, usually losing to plain one-hot. Hence, the generally useful part of Neural Collapse geometry in Analytic Continual Learning is equinorm post-processing of the weights, becoming more useful as class imbalance grows; and equiangularity is at best a no-op and induces catastrophic forgetting at worst.

items.title: Neuro-Inspired Inhibitory Message Passing for Accurate and Token-Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.raw_content:
Authors: Nima H. Siboni, Magdalena Springer, Vahid Rostami

Multi-agent systems promise to solve problems by bringing together information beyond the reach of any individual agent. Retrieval and tool use can distribute this information across agents, making communication essential to collaboration. A central challenge is keeping crucial evidence visible in each agent's context as messages accumulate. Repeated information can crowd out rare, decisive evidence. Models of cortical circuits suggest a principle for addressing this imbalance: inhibition can selectively suppress shared inputs while preserving sensitivity to weaker signals. We adapt this principle into inhibitory message passing, a training-free communication router that cancels redundant evidence separately for each evidence sentence and receiver. Each round, it forwards evidence sentences restated in agents' messages, delivering each at most once to receivers whose own evidence lacks it and excluding the senders' reasoning and answers. Against standard message passing, accuracy in peer groups rose by 39-77 percentage points across three benchmarks, and tokens per run fell by 10-46%. Gains held across seven open models spanning four to thirty-two billion parameters and two commercial models, in groups up to sixty-four agents, and across multi-agent architectures including peer-to-peer, orchestrator-worker, and multilevel hierarchical organizations. These findings support a scalable design pattern for more accurate and token-efficient multi-agent reasoning.

items.title: Peer Pressure: Execution-Verified Co-Evolution of Attacker and Defender Populations for Code Security
items.raw_content:
Authors: Khushbu Pahwa, Yubin Ge, Daniele Bonadiman, Xiaofei Ma, Yi Zhang

LLM code agents increasingly ship code with little oversight, yet defenders trained on static vulnerability datasets fall behind adapting adversaries. We co-train attacker and defender instead, and let execution decide every reward: an attacker (Red) edits a real repository and earns nothing unless its patch applies, builds, passes the tests, completes its development task and reproduces a real exploit in an isolated container, whose path also labels the entry point, the critical operation and the trace between them.
  Peer-Relative Policy Optimization (PRPO) makes both sides populations of LoRA adapters over one frozen base and credits each against same-role peers that faced an identical condition, placing the population inside the policy-gradient baseline rather than the opponent pool, with a tournament preserving diversity. Matching cancels the condition's difficulty: at equal coverage it is worth 2.3 points of balanced accuracy over a baseline computed on other conditions, and it matches a within-policy control at half the verifier spend.
  PRPO's 7B diff reviewer reaches 64.8% balanced accuracy on four unseen applications in three untrained languages, 5.5 points above supervised security fine-tuning and 4.4 above a frozen frontier reviewer (Claude Opus 4.8), which it leads by 15.8 on the application it trains on. Its 9B repository agent recovers 23 of 172 held-out VulnGym advisories, against 10 after supervised fine-tuning and 7 for the same backbone untrained under the same scaffold, and locates 17 of 43 reachable entry points against 13 for mini-swe-agent with GLM-5.2. Run unchanged on jailbreak defense, the same algorithm matches or exceeds WildGuard's static F1 at equal corpus and model size. Under a judge distinct from its training oracle it cuts attack success from 36.0% to 4.6%, against WildGuard's 8.9%.

items.title: A Symmetry-Matching Approach to Blind-Spot Reduction in Sparse Autoencoders
items.raw_content:
Authors: Csaba Balogh

Language models can treat semantically distinct inputs as interchangeable at the representation level, creating blind spots that standard sparse autoencoder (SAE) objectives do not target. In safety-critical settings such as clinical dosage extraction, legal clause interpretation, or financial amount verification, such failures can propagate silently into downstream decisions. We study this problem as one of feature-basis orientation. Building on a symmetry-matching view from algebraic error-detection theory, we add a differentiable $V_{\mathrm{Gini}}$ regularisation term to SAE training that penalises uneven perturbation response within a specified family. Across GPT-2, Gemma 2, and Qwen 2.5, a frozen multi-seed evaluation shows that $V$-regularisation raises both relative and absolute lower-tail responses while reducing response-profile imbalance, with no material general-text reconstruction degradation. JumpReLU and minimum description length (MDL) objectives remain close to the Standard SAE profile under the same protocol. Family-geometry controls show that the effect is not explained by template duplication or a single dominant perturbation family, and held-out probes plus null-calibrated separation tests evaluate how far the representation-level change carries to downstream discriminability. A zero-shot audit on out-of-distribution clinical radiology minimal pairs finds the relative weak-tail lift in all evaluated model-by-family cells, not perfectly rank-aligned with the trained statistic, and a held-out family audit finds it on family kinds never used in training. Together, the results show that perturbation-aware SAE training can reorient feature bases toward safety-relevant input changes while leaving downstream validation as a separate empirical step.

items.title: Arctic-SWE: Revisiting the Long Horizon Agent Training by Modeling-System Co-Design
items.title_zh: Arctic-SWE：以模型—系统协同设计重访长程智能体训练
items.raw_content: Arctic-SWE is a fully asynchronous reinforcement-learning framework that establishes a reproducible long-horizon agent baseline through model-system co-design. On raw R2E-Gym data it trains Qwen3.5-4B to 62.0% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified after about one-sixth as many rollouts as concurrent FrogNano, and with curated data the 4B model reaches 65.0% on SWE-bench Verified.

items.title: HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents
items.title_zh: HybridResearcher：打通结构化与非结构化边界的深度研究智能体
items.raw_content: HybridResearcher is a 4B agent trained to reason across structured and unstructured sources, built from synthesized cross-source trajectories and trained with supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. On the HybridDeepResearch benchmark it improves over its Qwen3.5-4B base by 30.0 points pass@8 and surpasses the larger Qwen3.5-397B-A17B by 8.3 points.

items.title: How Well Can LLMs Verbalize Mathematical Formulas? A Multi-Domain Evaluation
items.title_zh: LLM 能把数学公式读得多准？一项多领域评估
items.raw_content: The authors built Read-Aloud Math, a multi-domain corpus of LaTeX formulas with manually validated simple and extended transcriptions, and evaluated five LLMs on verbalizing them. GPT-5.2 scored highest on simple transcriptions (75.9% BLEU without context), while Claude Sonnet 4.5 led extended transcriptions without context and Grok 4.1 Fast with context, with results varying by domain and formula characteristics.
